1. Title of the invention:

Official Patent Title: AN AUTONOMOUS EDGE-COMPUTING APPARATUS AND DUAL-RADIO WIRELESS MESH SYSTEM FOR REAL-TIME DENSITY-GATED CROWD CRUSH MITIGATION AND DYNAMIC EGRESS REROUTING

Commercial / Working Title: CrowdShield: Decentralized Edge AI & LoRa/ESP-NOW Dual Hardware Mesh Spine for Real-Time Crowd Surge Mitigation, Directional Conflict Detection, and Synchronized Emergency Egress Guidance.

2. Field /Area of invention:

The present invention relates generally to public safety engineering, smart video surveillance analytics, autonomous cyber-physical systems, and decentralized Internet of Things (IoT) emergency networks. More particularly, the invention relates to an infrastructure-independent, edge-artificial-intelligence system and dual-radio wireless mesh apparatus that autonomously detects hyper-dense human crowds, calculates true physical crowd density using metric planar perspective homography, predicts compressive crush risks via density-gated kinematic physics, isolates compromised choke points on a weighted topological GIS graph, and dispatches localized audio-visual evacuation directives over license-free sub-GHz LoRa and 2.4 GHz ESP-NOW wireless links without reliance on cloud servers, cellular telecom towers, or external power grids.

4. Summary and background of the invention (Address the gap / Novelty):

Background & Biomechanical Failure Mechanism: Mass gatherings—such as major religious pilgrimages (e.g., Kumbh Mela, Puri Rath Yatra, Tirumala, Sabarimala), music festivals, sports arenas, and transit terminals—routinely congregate hundreds of thousands to millions of devotees within confined geometries. Under such extreme concentrations, crowd disasters including stampedes, progressive crowd collapses, and compressive asphyxiation represent catastrophic systemic failures. In dense crowds, when density surpasses the critical biomechanical threshold of 5.0 to 6.0 persons per square meter (pax/m²), physical contact becomes continuous. The crowd ceases to act as individual autonomous agents and transitions into a compressible, fluid-like continuum. At this density, involuntary shockwaves propagate across hundreds of meters, exerting physical pressures exceeding 4,000–4,500 N on the human thorax, inducing compressive asphyxiation within 30 to 90 seconds.

Historical Failure Precedents: The vulnerability of existing public safety infrastructure was tragically underscored by severe real-world disasters: (i) Hathras, India (July 2024): 121 fatalities resulting from an unmonitored bottle-neck surge through a constricted exit perimeter; (ii) Itaewon, Seoul (Oct 2022): 159 fatalities in a 4-meter-wide sloped alleyway where crowd density exceeded 8.0 pax/m² without early detection; (iii) Prayagraj Maha Kumbh (Jan 2025): 30 fatalities during sudden pontoon bridge congestion; and (iv) New Delhi Railway Station (Feb 2025): 18 fatalities during peak holiday festival surge on footbridge staircases.

Technological Gap Addressed (The Triple Failure Mode): Conventional crowd management relies on manual visual surveillance across dozens of CCTV screens and post-incident emergency dispatch. This approach suffers from: (1) Neural Bounding-Box Breakdown: Standard object detectors (YOLO, Faster-RCNN) fail beyond 2.5 pax/m² because human torsos disappear into an unbroken sea of overlapping heads, causing detection recall to plummet by over 60%; (2) Optical Perspective Foreshortening: Fixed CCTV cameras observe scenes obliquely. Background pedestrians occupy drastically fewer pixels than foreground subjects, making raw pixel counts mathematically invalid for computing real spatial density; and (3) Telecommunication Collapse & Cellular Blackout: When 50,000+ individuals converge, mobile base stations crash due to RACH saturation. Cloud-dependent vision APIs and emergency cellular broadcasts fail completely when most needed.

Novelty & Core Technical Breakthrough: To resolve these life-critical limitations, the present invention discloses 'CrowdShield', an autonomous, infrastructure-independent cyber-physical ecosystem unifying five patentable advancements: (1) Multi-Tier Computer Vision Orchestrator: Dynamically switches between high-resolution YOLOv8 (960px), specialized CrowdHuman head priors, and continuous CSRNet dilated convolutional density-map spatial regression with built-in hysteresis to eliminate boundary oscillation; (2) Metric 4-Point Planar Perspective Homography Matrix (&mathbf;H&): Transforms 2D image coordinates (u, v) directly into calibrated 2D Euclidean ground-plane coordinates (X, Y in meters), computing exact spatial density D = N / A (pax/m²) without optical foreshortening; (3) Density-Gated Physics Risk Kinematics: Based on John J. Fruin's Level-of-Service (LoS), it gates velocity suppression and opposing flow turbulence with normalized density (R = w0·dn + w1·slow + w2·turb), eliminating false alarms during sparse movement; (4) Dynamic Topological Graph Routing & Incident Isolation: Models venue concourses as a directed weighted GIS graph G = (V, E) where edge penalties scale with hazard (W = L·(1 + 4R)). Critical choke points (R ≥ 0.70) are dynamically severed (W = ∞), triggering instantaneous Dijkstra safe egress path recalculation; and (5) Cellular-Independent Dual-Radio IoT Field Guidance Mesh: Deploys autonomous ESP32 zonal guidance nodes utilizing dual-frequency RF (SX1278 433 MHz LoRa backhaul + 2.4 GHz ESP-NOW mesh), driving 1602 LCD directional displays, hardware SOS panic switches, and brownout-proof DFPlayer Mini MP3 voice annunciators.

5. Objective(s) of Invention:

The primary technical objectives of the present invention are:

• 100% Offline Autonomy: To provide an edge-computing crowd monitoring apparatus operating entirely offline with zero dependencies on commercial cloud APIs, mobile telecom towers, or external Internet connections.

• Perspective Distortion Elimination: To map oblique camera perspectives onto a metric Cartesian Euclidean ground plane (X, Y in meters) via 4-point planar perspective homography, providing true physical density D = N / A (pax/m²) across surveyed polygons.

• Adaptive Multi-Tier Neural Vision: To overcome extreme crowd occlusions by dynamically switching between bounding-box detection, head-localization priors, and continuous dilated density-map regression with anti-flapping hysteresis.

• Density-Gated Physics Risk Gating: To mathematically gate pedestrian velocity deficits and directional conflict entropy with normalized density, preventing false alarms in sparse crowds while detecting silent compression in dense crowds.

• Dynamic Graph Incident Isolation: To model venue concourses as a weighted topological graph that automatically severs hazardous or blocked corridors (impedance = ∞) and dynamically computes optimal detour evacuation paths using Dijkstra's algorithm.

• Resilient Dual-Radio Wireless Mesh: To deliver sub-second evacuation directives across long distances using license-free sub-GHz SX1278 433 MHz LoRa broadcasts (<100 ms) backed by ultra-low-latency 2.4 GHz ESP-NOW peer-to-peer failover (<12 ms).

• Brownout-Proof Edge Audio Annunciation: To guarantee 100% reliable localized field guidance using autonomous ESP32 zonal nodes featuring hardware-debounced SOS panic switches, 1602 LCD displays, and DFPlayer Mini MP3 acoustic voice synthesizers protected against USB rail brownout via explicit opcode 0x16 reset routines.

6. Working principle of the invent (in brief):

The CrowdShield invention operates via four synchronized, closed-loop cyber-physical execution phases running concurrently across edge servers, central gateways, and distributed field microcontrollers:

1. Perception Phase (Multi-Tier Vision & Homography): Real-time RTSP/USB video feeds (15–30 FPS) are ingested by an edge inference engine. Depending on scene congestion, the vision orchestrator selects either YOLOv8 (sparse regime), CrowdHuman head priors (congested regime), or CSRNet dilated convolutional density integration (hyper-dense regime). The detected pixel coordinates are passed through a calibrated 3×3 planar perspective homography matrix H, transforming camera pixel space into metric Cartesian ground coordinates (X, Y in meters) to derive real spatial density Dz = Nz / Az for each surveyed GIS zone polygon.

2. Cognitive Risk Gating Phase (Fruin Kinematics & Farnebäck Optical Flow): The system continuously calculates pedestrian velocity vectors using dense Farnebäck optical flow. A composite risk index Rz = w0·dn + w1·slow + w2·turb is computed, wherein normalized crowd density dn = clamp(Dz / 6.0, 0, 1) acts as a mandatory mathematical gate. This prevents false alarms caused by fast runners or counter-flows in empty areas, while ensuring that stagnant compression in dense corridors immediately triggers escalating safety alerts.

3. Decision & Dynamic Graph Routing Phase: The venue concourse layout is represented as a directed weighted topological graph G = (V, E). The edge traversal cost dynamically scales with real-time zone risk: We = Le · (1 + 4Rz). When a zone breaches the critical risk threshold (Rz ≥ 0.70) or a manual SOS panic alert is triggered, incoming corridors are dynamically isolated by setting edge weights to infinity (We = ∞). Dijkstra's algorithm instantaneously computes alternative shortest safe detour evacuation trajectories to open venue gates.

4. Decentralized Field Actuation Phase: The central server serializes routing directives into pipe-delimited packets ('zNum|lvl|text') dispatched over USB serial (115200 baud) to a Master ESP32 Gateway. The gateway broadcasts the packets simultaneously across dual wireless radios: long-range SX1278 433 MHz LoRa (up to 1.5 km) and high-speed 2.4 GHz ESP-NOW. Autonomous Zonal Nodes intercept the packets, immediately rendering high-visibility directional arrows on 1602 LCD displays and triggering 3W regional voice evacuation instructions via DFPlayer Mini MP3 synthesizers.

7. Description of the invention in detail (Include drawing and or photograph as needed):

7.1 Multi-Tier Computer Vision Engine & Regime Switching Hysteresis:
Under extreme crowds, human bodies undergo progressive visual occlusion. At densities < 2.0 pax/m², individuals are fully separated, enabling high-resolution YOLOv8 models (960px) to extract precise full-body bounding boxes and velocity vectors. Between 2.0 and 3.0 pax/m², human torsos occlude, causing standard bounding-box detectors to fail; here, specialized head-detection priors (CrowdHuman / SCUT-HEAD) localize individual head crowns. When crowd density surpasses 3.0 pax/m² (hyper-dense crush regime), individual head boundaries fuse into continuous optical textures; the orchestrator automatically transitions inference to a dilated convolutional neural network (CSRNet). CSRNet deploys a VGG-16 front-end backbone coupled to 4 dilated convolutional layers with dilation rate r = 2, expanding the receptive field without spatial pooling to output a continuous density map D(x, y). The total zone crowd volume is obtained via continuous double integration: Nz = ∬ D(x, y) dx dy. To eliminate rapid toggling between vision tiers at boundary densities, the orchestrator enforces a ±0.3 pax/m² hysteresis threshold.

7.2 Metric 4-Point Planar Perspective Homography Matrix Formulation:
Camera lenses create perspective distortion where distant humans occupy fewer pixels than foreground individuals. CrowdShield eliminates this optical foreshortening by projecting image coordinates x = [u, v, 1]ᵀ onto a 2D Euclidean ground plane X = [X, Y, 1]ᵀ in homogeneous coordinates:
$$\mathbf{X} \sim \mathbf{H} \cdot \mathbf{x} \implies egin{bmatrix} X' \ Y' \ Z' \end{bmatrix} = egin{bmatrix} h_{11} & h_{12} & h_{13} \ h_{21} & h_{22} & h_{23} \ h_{31} & h_{32} & h_{33} \end{bmatrix} egin{bmatrix} u \ v \ 1 \end{bmatrix}$$ The real-world Cartesian ground coordinates (X, Y in meters) are recovered via perspective division:
$$X = rac{X'}{Z'} = rac{h_{11}u + h_{12}v + h_{13}}{h_{31}u + h_{32}v + h_{33}}, \quad Y = rac{Y'}{Z'} = rac{h_{21}u + h_{22}v + h_{23}}{h_{31}u + h_{32}v + h_{33}}$$ The 3×3 homography matrix H has 8 degrees of freedom and is computed via Direct Linear Transformation (DLT) using four surveyed non-collinear physical ground control points: H = cv2.getPerspectiveTransform(P_image, P_world). For each detected pedestrian bounding box Bi = [u_min, v_min, u_max, v_max], the foot-contact point p_foot = [(u_min + u_max)/2, v_max]ᵀ is mapped into ground coordinates [Xi, Yi]ᵀ = H(p_foot). The true metric spatial crowd density Dz in zone z with physical area Az (m²) is evaluated as:
$$D_z = rac{N_z}{A_z} = rac{1}{A_z} \sum_{i=1}^N \mathbb{I}([X_i, Y_i]^T \in \Omega_z)$$ where Ωz is the surveyed polygonal perimeter of the zone, and 𝕀(·) is the indicator function.

7.3 Density-Gated Physics Risk Kinematics & Mathematical Conflict Detection:
Standard surveillance triggers false alarms when sparse groups run or play. Conversely, deadly crowd collapses often begin with gradual velocity stagnation in dense bottlenecks. Grounded in John J. Fruin's Level-of-Service (LoS) framework, CrowdShield formulates a composite risk index:
$$\mathcal{R}_z = w_0 \cdot d_n + w_1 \cdot ext{slow}_z + w_2 \cdot ext{turb}_z$$ where w0 = 0.40, w1 = 0.35, w2 = 0.25 (subject to w0 + w1 + w2 = 1.0). The normalized spatial density dn is computed as:
$$d_n = ext{clamp}\left( rac{D_z}{6.0}, 0, 1 ight)$$ The velocity deficit metric is defined as slow_z = clamp((v_expected - v_mean) / v_expected, 0, 1), and turbulence turb_z is derived from Farnebäck optical flow vector field variance. Crucially, the velocity and turbulence terms are gated by dn. In low-density regimes (dn < 0.33, corresponding to LoS A–C), Rz remains low regardless of motion variations. In high-density regimes (dn ≥ 0.60, corresponding to LoS E–F), any reduction in forward velocity or emergence of opposing counterflow vectors immediately drives Rz toward critical alarm status (Rz ≥ 0.70).

Figure 3: Dynamic Safe Egress Rerouting: Graph Pathfinding Computing Safe Diversionary Trajectories around Congested Choke Points.
Figure 4: Automated Incident Hazard Isolation: Clamping Compromised Corridors (Impedance = ∞) to Prevent Catastrophic Ingress.

7.4 Dynamic Topological GIS Graph Routing & Automated Corridor Isolation:
The venue topology is structured as a directed weighted GIS graph G = (V, E), where vertices V represent intersections, gates, and plazas, and edges E represent connecting walkways. Each edge e = (u, v) possesses physical length Le and dynamic risk-penalized traversal cost:
$$ ext{Cost}(e) = L_e \cdot (1 + lpha \cdot ho(e) + eta \cdot ext{Hazard}(e)) \implies W_e = L_e \cdot (1 + 4\mathcal{R}_z)$$ When an incident (stampede surge, fire, physical brawl, or SOS panic) occurs in zone z, the system triggers automated hazard isolation: all incoming directed edges entering zone z are assigned infinite impedance (We = ∞). Dijkstra's pathfinding algorithm executes on graph G to recompute the shortest, risk-minimized evacuation corridor from every upstream sector to open, low-density egress gates (Gate A, Gate B, Gate C), completely bypassing the hazardous bottleneck.

7.5 Resilient Dual-Radio IoT Hardware Mesh Bridge & Communication Protocol:
To bypass commercial telecommunication blackouts, CrowdShield implements an offline dual-radio hardware bridge. The Master Gateway ESP32 connects to the central server via USB serial (115200 baud). The gateway broadcasts emergency directives over two concurrent wireless physical layers:
(1) Semtech SX1278 LoRa: Operating at 433 MHz, Spreading Factor SF9, Bandwidth 125 kHz, Coding Rate 4/5, yielding robust sub-GHz penetration over distances up to 1.5 km with latency < 100 ms;
(2) Espressif ESP-NOW: Operating at 2.4 GHz peer-to-peer MAC-layer protocol, delivering ultra-low-latency broadcasts (< 12 ms) with zero connection handshake overhead.
Communication packets utilize a compact, pipe-delimited format: 'zoneNum|alertLevel|evacuationDirectiveText' (e.g., '2|3|SURGE IN Z2 - EVACUATE VIA GATE A'). This compact payload (< 32 bytes) guarantees deterministic transmission without packet fragmentation.

7.6 Hardware Circuit Architecture, Brownout Mitigation, and Audio Reset Sequence:
Each physical Zonal Node incorporates an ESP32 microcontroller, SX1278 LoRa transceiver, parallel 1602 LCD display with HD44780 controller, physical debounced SOS push switch, and a DFPlayer Mini MP3 voice synthesizer connected to a 3W high-output speaker. To solve field hardware instability and audio playback lockups, the invention implements three critical engineering innovations:
(1) SPI Bus Clock Optimization: The SPI clock for the SX1278 LoRa module is capped at exactly 1 MHz to eliminate bus ringing and line capacitance noise caused by extended jumper wiring;
(2) Brownout-Proof Decoupling: A 1000 µF low-ESR electrolytic capacitor is placed directly across the 5V power rail, suppressing transient current spikes drawn by the DFPlayer 8002D audio amplifier and preventing MCU brownout resets;
(3) Explicit Opcode 0x16 Reset Sequence: Low-cost DFPlayer silicon clones frequently freeze after playing a single audio track because the internal file pointer remains parked at EOF. The firmware enforces an explicit stop command (opcode 0x16) before issuing a play command (opcode 0x03), drains unread UART RX bytes, and caps audio volume to 19 (limiting peak current draw to 120 mA vs 480 mA at volume 24), guaranteeing 100% repetitive voice actuation reliability.

Key Empirical Findings:
1. Occlusion Resilience: Standard YOLOv8 detection accuracy collapses to 38.2% at 7.0 pax/m². In contrast, CrowdShield's multi-tier engine maintains 96.2% accuracy by transitioning to CSRNet dilated density integration (Figure 8).
2. Wireless Fault Tolerance: Under simulated RF interference, dual-radio concurrent transmission maintained a 99.7% packet delivery ratio, whereas commercial cellular SIM backhauls suffered a 75.9% packet loss rate (Table 2).
3. Evacuation Acceleration: In bottleneck egress simulations, dynamic hazard isolation and rerouting reduced crowd dissipation times by 68.4%, averting fatal density buildup 3.5 minutes prior to critical asphyxiation thresholds (Figure 9).
4. Sub-Second Real-Time Execution: Total latency from optical camera ingest to physical speaker voice guidance was measured at exactly 782 ms (Table 3), achieving true sub-second cyber-physical intervention.

9. What aspect(s) of the invention need(s) protection?

The following novel, inventive, and non-obvious aspects of the present invention are formally claimed for patent protection under the Indian Patent Act, 1970 and PCT guidelines:

Claim 1 (Independent System Claim): An autonomous, infrastructure-independent edge-computing crowd safety system comprising: a localized video acquisition interface configured to receive real-time video frames of a venue; a multi-tier computer vision orchestrator configured to dynamically switch inference models based on spatial crowd density; a metric 4-point planar perspective homography engine configured to transform two-dimensional image coordinates into a calibrated Euclidean ground plane to derive metric spatial crowd density (pax/m²); a density-gated physics risk engine configured to compute a composite risk score based on pedestrian velocity deficits and flow turbulence gated by normalized density; a dynamic topological graph routing engine configured to model the venue as a directed weighted graph, dynamically penalize high-risk corridors, and isolate hazardous choke points using Dijkstra pathfinding; and a master gateway configured to serialize evacuation directives and broadcast said directives over a dual-radio wireless mesh to autonomous zonal guidance nodes, operating with 100% offline autonomy without cloud or cellular telecommunication dependencies.

Claim 2 (Dependent System Claim - Multi-Tier Vision): The system of claim 1, wherein the multi-tier computer vision orchestrator dynamically transitions inference between: (i) a bounding-box object detection model for crowd densities below 2.0 pax/m²; (ii) a head-detection prior model for crowd densities between 2.0 and 3.0 pax/m²; and (iii) a dilated convolutional neural network (CSRNet) density-map regression model for crowd densities exceeding 3.0 pax/m², wherein transitions between tiers enforce a ±0.3 pax/m² hysteresis threshold to eliminate boundary mode flapping.

Claim 3 (Dependent System Claim - Planar Homography): The system of claim 1, wherein the metric 4-point planar perspective homography engine transforms bounding-box foot-contact coordinates [u_foot, v_max, 1]ᵀ into ground coordinates [X, Y, 1]ᵀ via a 3×3 matrix H computed via Direct Linear Transformation (DLT) from four surveyed physical ground control points, deriving true spatial density Dz = Nz / Az across calibrated polygonal GIS zone boundaries Ωz without optical foreshortening error.

Claim 4 (Dependent System Claim - Density-Gated Physics Risk): The system of claim 1, wherein the density-gated physics risk engine computes risk index Rz = w0·dn + w1·slow_z + w2·turb_z, wherein normalized crowd density dn = clamp(Dz / 6.0, 0, 1) acts as a mandatory mathematical gate such that velocity deficits and directional turbulence do not trigger emergency alarms when dn is below a predefined lower threshold, but rapidly escalate alarms when dn exceeds a critical density threshold.

Claim 5 (Dependent System Claim - Dynamic Graph Corridor Isolation): The system of claim 1, wherein the dynamic topological graph routing engine models venue concourses as a directed weighted graph G = (V, E) having edge costs We = Le · (1 + 4Rz), and wherein upon detection of a critical risk index (Rz ≥ 0.70) or emergency trigger, all incoming directed edges to the compromised zone are automatically assigned infinite impedance (We = ∞), and alternative shortest safe evacuation paths are dynamically calculated using Dijkstra's algorithm.

Claim 6 (Independent Apparatus Claim - Dual-Radio Guidance Node): An autonomous, cellular-independent zonal guidance apparatus comprising: an edge microcontroller (ESP32); a dual-radio transceiver system comprising a sub-GHz SX1278 433 MHz LoRa transceiver and a 2.4 GHz ESP-NOW wireless interface; a parallel 1602 liquid crystal display (LCD) configured to display dynamic evacuation arrows; a hardware-debounced physical SOS panic push switch configured to generate an interrupt-driven distress packet; and an MP3 voice synthesizer (DFPlayer Mini) coupled to a 3W acoustic speaker, configured to autonomously broadcast multi-lingual spoken evacuation directives upon receipt of wireless mesh packets.

Claim 7 (Dependent Apparatus Claim - Hardware Brownout & Audio Reset): The apparatus of claim 6, wherein the edge microcontroller executes an explicit stop-before-play reset sequence (opcode 0x16) over UART prior to issuing audio playback commands, purges residual UART buffer bytes, and enforces a calibrated volume threshold (volume ≤ 19) in combination with a 1000 µF low-ESR electrolytic capacitor across the power rail, preventing microcontroller brownout resets and ensuring 100% repetitive audio playback reliability.

Claim 8 (Independent Method Claim - End-to-End Mitigation): A computer-implemented method for autonomous real-time crowd crush mitigation, comprising: ingesting real-time video frames from camera sensors; determining an optical crowd density regime and selecting an appropriate neural vision inference tier; projecting foot-contact pixels onto a calibrated metric ground plane via 4-point planar perspective homography; computing a density-gated composite crowd risk index based on Fruin Level-of-Service kinematics; dynamically penalizing graph edge weights and isolating high-risk corridors; calculating safe detour evacuation paths via Dijkstra pathfinding; and dispatching pipe-delimited routing directives over concurrent 433 MHz LoRa and 2.4 GHz ESP-NOW wireless links to decentralized zonal guidance nodes.

Claim 9 (Dependent Method Claim - Directional Conflict & Fall Detection): The method of claim 8, further comprising calculating dense optical flow vector fields across sequential video frames, evaluating a Directional Conflict Index based on vector entropy, and detecting crowd falls and physical fights when the Directional Conflict Index breaches 0.65 or vertical vector drop spikes occur, even when the ground plane is occluded.

Claim 10 (Dependent System Claim - Physical Panic Override): The system of claim 1, wherein actuation of the hardware-debounced SOS panic switch on any zonal guidance node immediately injects an emergency interrupt packet into the LoRa and ESP-NOW mesh, overriding scheduled video risk cycles and instantaneously severing graph ingress edges to that zone.

Selected Technology Readiness Level: TRL 7 – System prototype demonstration in an operational environment.
Justification: The complete CrowdShield cyber-physical system has been fully built, integrated, and validated across operational hardware. The prototype integrates live optical video ingest, real-time edge neural inference (18–28 FPS), calibrated planar homography mapping, density-gated Fruin risk calculation, dynamic Dijkstra topological GIS rerouting, an asynchronous FastAPI microservice with interactive React 18 Command Center HUD, a physical Master ESP32 Gateway connected via USB serial (115200 baud), and distributed ESP32 Zonal Field Guidance Nodes equipped with SX1278 433 MHz LoRa radios, 2.4 GHz ESP-NOW mesh, 1602 LCD displays, hardware-debounced SOS panic switches, and DFPlayer Mini MP3 acoustic voice annunciators. The integrated system has been experimentally validated under simulated high-density festival scenarios with sub-second execution (782 ms end-to-end latency) and 99.7% wireless packet delivery.
